functional_sequences.title: Air pressure to cochlear motion
functional_sequences.mechanism: Pressure oscillations become mechanical displacement at the cochlear partition.

steps.caption: Sound pressure oscillates in the canal and drives the tympanic membrane.
The malleus couples to the membrane; the incus and stapes transmit its motion through their joints.
Membrane-to-footplate area and ossicular leverage increase pressure delivered to fluid; they do not create acoustic energy.
The stapes footplate displaces perilymph through the oval window. The compliant round window permits compensating displacement.
Scala vestibuli and scala tympani contain perilymph; the enclosed cochlear duct contains endolymph. Reissner and basilar membranes preserve separation.
The cochlear partition supports a traveling wave. Higher frequencies peak toward the base; lower frequencies peak toward the apex.
The magnified cochlear inset exposes the sensory apparatus carried by the basilar membrane.

schematic_limitations: Static anatomical states, no calibrated oscillation or pressure magnitude.
Fluid colors identify compartments; they do not measure ionic concentration or pressure.
The helicotrema joins the perilymphatic scalae at the apex; there is no circulating bolus of sound that must travel there before transduction.
The inset is one representative cochlear turn; it does not calculate frequency-specific peaks or tuning.

functional_sequences.title: Bundle deflection to auditory afferent signal
functional_sequences.mechanism: Hair-cell receptor potentials and synaptic release connect cochlear mechanics to neural signaling.

steps.caption: The stria vascularis maintains the endolymph environment. Hair bundles face endolymph while the sensory epithelial barrier preserves ionic separation.
Relative motion of the sensory surface and overlying tectorial membrane bends the stereocilia.
Deflection toward the tallest stereocilia raises mechanotransduction-channel opening; inward cation current, chiefly potassium, depolarizes the hair cell.
Depolarization opens basal voltage-gated calcium channels and promotes transmitter release onto afferent terminals. The hair cell produces a receptor potential.
Spiral ganglion afferents generate action potentials. Inner hair cells provide most auditory afferent input.
Outer hair-cell prestin supports rapid voltage-dependent length change and mechanical amplification. This assists sensitivity and frequency selectivity.
Peripheral fibres connect to spiral ganglion neurons; their central axons join the cochlear nerve and then cranial nerve VIII.

schematic_limitations: Tip links, ion channels, synaptic vesicles and prestin molecules are described; they are not separate mesh parts.
The shared stereocilia part prevents independent selection of each hair-cell bundle.
Inner hair-cell bundles are not shown as rigidly embedded in the tectorial membrane; local fluid coupling differs from outer hair-cell tallest-bundle contact.
No cell deformation, ionic-current meter, voltage trace, neural firing rate or acoustic threshold is simulated.
Cell counts and microscopic sizes are enlarged representative samples, with no adult human total-count inference.

functional_sequences.title: Rotation, endolymph inertia and cupula
functional_sequences.mechanism: Changes in head rotation produce relative endolymph motion that loads the cupula and alters vestibular afferent activity.

steps.caption: Each semicircular duct has an ampulla containing a crista and cupula. Three duct planes provide complementary rotation sensitivity.
At rotation onset, endolymph initially lags the moving duct. Its relative motion loads the cupula, which spans the ampullary lumen.
Bundles embedded in the cupula bend together. Deflection toward the kinocilium raises afferent activity; deflection away lowers it.
Bundles in one crista share directional polarity. A coplanar canal on the other side normally supplies a complementary push-pull response.
During prolonged constant angular velocity the cupula tends back toward neutral and peripheral firing approaches baseline; rotation can continue.
Deceleration can produce an opposite transient cupular deflection and afferent change before the response settles.

schematic_limitations: The right-ear model contains no left partner; bilateral push-pull is captioned context.
The magnified crista is a generic crest with consistently oriented bundles; it is not a calibrated horizontal, anterior or posterior canal stimulus map.
Do not infer excitation from screen-left or screen-right: use the local kinocilium direction.
The normal cupula has no otoconial load.
No angular acceleration, duration, cupular displacement, fluid streamlines or firing values are assigned.

functional_sequences.title: Utricle, saccule and loaded otolithic membrane
functional_sequences.mechanism: Otoconial mass couples gravity and translational inertia to macular hair-bundle shear.

steps.caption: With the head upright, the utricular macula is predominantly horizontal and the saccular macula predominantly vertical. Each samples a range of bundle directions.
Attached calcium-carbonate otoconia load the otolithic membrane above the gelatinous layer and sensory epithelium.
During translation the loaded layer lags relative to the sensory epithelium. Gel coupling shears the bundles and alters receptor potentials.
Head tilt changes gravitational loading of the membrane. Otolith signals alone cannot uniquely distinguish gravity from translational acceleration.
This representative utricular strip has kinocilia toward its polarity-reversal boundary. A shared shear excites one domain and inhibits the other.
The saccular macula has the opposite polarity arrangement: bundles face away from the reversal boundary. The displayed utricular inset must not substitute for a saccular map.
Macular afferents connect through vestibular ganglion neurons and the vestibular nerve to cranial nerve VIII.

schematic_limitations: The macular inset is a planar representative utricular strip, not a map of the entire human macula.
The line of polarity reversal is a schematic boundary; it is not a separate membrane or synonymous with the full striolar zone.
The source uses mixed scales and 36 enlarged representative crystals, not physiological crystal dimensions or counts.
Grouped gross maculae and otolithic material do not permit independent utricular/saccular cell-level selection.
Otoconia are attached physiological load; no normal free-particle circulation or BPPV maneuver is animated.
Tilt/translation disambiguation requires central integration beyond this model.

functional_sequences.title: Air pressure equalization across the tympanic membrane
functional_sequences.mechanism: Auditory-tube gas exchange regulates the mean pressure of the middle-ear cavity.

steps.caption: The membrane separates external canal air from middle-ear air. Similar mean pressure on both sides supports normal mechanical motion.
Air passes between nasopharynx and middle ear through the auditory tube; swallowing or yawning can promote equalization.
If mean middle-ear pressure falls below canal pressure, the membrane tends to retract toward the middle ear; excess pressure tends to bulge it outward.
Mean air-pressure equalization through the tube differs from oscillatory fluid displacement at the oval and round windows during hearing.

schematic_limitations: No membrane retraction or tube opening is physically deformed; each state is explained on preserved anatomy.
Tensor veli palatini, nasopharyngeal cavity and tubal valve mechanics are outside the 104-part model.
No equalization maneuver, medication or management advice is prescribed.

view_notes.Overview: Right ear viewed from anterior. Gross anatomy is at 1 unit = 40 mm; three separately magnified teaching insets are hidden. The source is already a coronal dissection; viewer cut is off.
view_notes.Ossicular chain: Follow pars tensa to malleus, incus, stapes and footplate in the oval window. Keep both synovial joints, four ligaments, two muscles and their tendons; chorda tympani is a nearby nerve, not a sound-transmitting link. Gross scale preserved; tympanic membrane is thicker than life.
view_notes.Labyrinth fluids: Perilymph and endolymph are separate filled teaching domains. Follow the vestibule and cochlear scalae while identifying the cochlear duct, vestibular membrane and basilar membrane; retain the vestibular ducts and sensory patches. Gross scale preserved; membranes and spiral organ are thicker than life.
view_notes.Cochlear transduction: One separately magnified cochlear turn. Identify scala vestibuli, cochlear duct endolymph and scala tympani before following basilar membrane, hair cells, stereocilia, tectorial membrane and nerve fibres. Inset approximately x8; organ of Corti/cells have further enlargement. Native scale bar measures displayed model distance, not original tissue distance.
view_notes.Canal rotation: Crista ampullaris inset: cupula, sensory epithelium, Type I/II hair cells, supporting cells, stereocilia/kinocilia and ampullary nerve fibres. Inset approximately x10 with cells further enlarged. Review rotation in gross labyrinth first; the inset is a local section, not a rotating canal.
view_notes.Utricular loading: Macula inset: identify lamina propria, hair cells and supporting cells, then gelatinous layer, otolithic membrane, otoconia and nerve fibres. Representative local macular section used for utricular loading teaching; no patient-specific striola or whole-macula polarity map. Inset approximately x10; cells/crystals further enlarged; 36 crystals are schematic.
view_notes.Pressure equalization: Follow the tympanic cavity into the pharyngotympanic tube and tubal cartilage; mastoid antrum/representative air cells remain for context. Pressure equalization is a function sequence, not a fluid mesh deformation. Gross scale preserved; mastoid cell size/count are schematic.
view_notes.Auricle: External ear: preserve cartilage-backed folds, cartilage-free lobule, concha and S-shaped meatus. Gross scale 1 unit = 40 mm. Ceruminous/sebaceous gland units are enlarged representatives. Additional viewer clipping is available interactively but is off in this pose.

summary: A right-ear coronal teaching dissection with preserved external, middle and inner anatomy. Eight focused native views link air conduction, ossicular pressure transfer, cochlear transduction and vestibular sensing. The macular inset represents a schematic utricular patch.
scale_note: Drawn to scale, 1 model unit = 40 mm: the auricle is ~62 mm tall, the meatus ~24 mm long, the cochlea ~9 mm across and the stapes ~3 mm. The tympanic membrane, the membranous labyrinth and the spiral organ are drawn a little thicker than life. Insets: cochlear duct ~x8, crista and macula ~x10, with their cells further enlarged. Representative counts and straight macular polarity boundary are schematic; the macular inset illustrates utricular polarity, not a whole-macula map.
